title: Migration Acceleration Lifecycle Playbook: Dedicated → Private + SLA
content:
Purpose:
Deliver a compact, repeatable playbook for accelerating conversions from Dedicated to Private deployments and for selling premium SLA add-ons during renewal windows. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — contains scripts, a six-week sprint, quick ROI worksheet, technical validation steps, and QBR prompts.

Audience:
- CSMs working top-of-funnel and renewal motions for mid-market + enterprise accounts
- Solutions engineers and AMs pairing on technical and procurement blockers
- Renewal & expansion ops for tracking commitments and risks

Success metrics (suggested):
- Conversion rate: Dedicated → Private within 12 months >= 18% for accounts flagged as 'migration-eligible'
- Time-to-contract: median 8–10 weeks from kickoff to signature for Private conversions
- SLA attach rate at renewal >= 40% for eligible accounts
- NRR contribution: expansion motions contribute +10% NRR in target cohort

Prereqs before kickoff:
- Current Dedicated contract and utilization report (last 90d tokens, peak RPS, 99th pct latency)
- Security questionnaire status and outstanding controls list
- Procurement cadence and primary procurement contact identified
- Initial risk tier (low/medium/high) assigned by CSM

Quick-risk checklist (SE):
- Data residency requirements? (yes/no)
- Encryption at-rest & KMS in scope? (yes/no)
- Network topology constraints (VPC peering, private link, air-gapped)?
- Regulatory constraints: HIPAA, SOC2, PCI, or local laws?
- Is on-prem deployment a possibility or strictly cloud VPC?

6-week migration-acceleration sprint (high-level):
Week 0 — Intake & alignment
- Meeting: CSM + SE + procurement + engineering stakeholder. Goal: shared success metrics and timeline.
- Deliverable: Project charter (one-pager) with acceptance criteria and Go/No-Go signals.

Week 1 — Security & compliance fast-path
- Run the security checklist (3rd-party attestation summary).
- If KMS/HSM required, identify integration owner and map key lifecycle.
- Deliverable: Security sign-off stub or list of gating items.

Week 2 — Proof-of-concept (PoC) plan + cost model
- SE builds a mini PoC runbook: model(s), sequence lengths, sample traffic.
- CSM prepares a 12-month cost comparison (Dedicated baseline vs Private with reserved commit + SLA premium). See ROI worksheet below.

Week 3 — PoC execution
- Run PoC with 2 representative workloads (light/peak) and capture latency, token cost, error rates.
- Capture screenshots/logs for QBR and procurement.

Week 4 — Procurement & contract template review
- Pull legal playbook: SLAs, indemnities, data handling clauses.
- AE/procurement present the minimum contract terms; negotiate scope and exit clauses.

Week 5 — Rollout plan & runbook handoff
- Create operational runbook: autoscaling settings, observability dashboards, runbook for failover to hosted model variants.
- Capture rollback criteria and escalation path.

Week 6 — Executive summary & signature roadmap
- Create a one-slide exec summary for sponsoring stakeholder (cost delta, timeline, ROI).
- Final negotiation and signature.

QBR talking points (script snippets):
- Usage: "Last quarter you averaged X tokens/day with Y 99p latency — Private will provide predictable throughput at Z% lower per-token cost under your commit."
- Reliability: "Private + SLA moves you from best-effort availability to 99.9%+ backed by credits and 24/7 incident support."
- Security: "VPC/private control plane lets you keep networking and KMS within your environment."
- Migration ask: "We need a 6-week technical validation window and a named procurement owner to make the timeline realistic."

Mini ROI worksheet (text form — CSM fills in numbers):
- Current monthly cost (Dedicated): [A] USD
- Estimated monthly cost (Private, reserved + ops): [B] USD
- SLA premium: [S]% of B => [S_amt] USD
- Projected monthly savings or delta: (A - (B + S_amt)) => [Delta] USD
- 12-month delta => [Delta]*12 => [YearDelta] USD
- Soft benefits: predictable latency improvements (qualitative), reduced throttling incidents, compliance readiness (list)

Common objections & rebuttals (CSM + SE pair):
- "We don’t want vendor-managed infra." => "Private offers a customer-managed control plane option; we can scope network handoff and provide runbook for your infra team."
- "Cost looks higher." => "Show the 12-month committed pricing vs uncommitted Dedicated burst pricing; call out predictable TCO for peak workloads and SLA credit protections."
- "KMS/HSM integration is a blocker." => "Bring our security SME to a 30-minute call; we have templates for common KMS providers and onboarding checklists."

Renewal tracker template (plain text columns to paste into a sheet):
- Account, Current Contract End, Eligible for Private, Migration Phase (intake/PoC/procurement/contracted), Estimated Close Date, Owner (CSM), SE Lead, Risk (L/M/H), Last Touch Notes

Email templates (short):
- Intro to procurement:
  Subject: Next steps for Private deployment evaluation
  Body: "Hi <ProcurementName>, pleased to meet you. We ran initial utilization reports and proposed a 6-week technical validation to demonstrate Private’s performance and compliance fit. Proposed owners: <CSM>, <SE>. Are you available for a 30-minute alignment this week?"

- Post-PoC executive summary (attach runbook/scorecard):
  Subject: PoC results — Private validation for <AccountName>
  Body: "Summary: PoC validated throughput X, median latency Y, error rate Z. Next steps: contract review and procurement kickoff. Attached: scorecard and one-slide ROI."

Handoff checklist to delivery/SRE:
- Confirm reserved capacity size and autoscaling policy
- Confirm monitoring endpoints & alert thresholds (token error rate > X, p95 latency > Y)
- Knowledge transfer session scheduled + recording
- Access matrix for keys and VPC peering documented

Open questions / things to improve (rough):
- Can we standardize a single contract amendment that covers most customers (reduces legal turnaround)?
- Do we need a smaller, lighter PoC option for customers who cannot run traffic? (suggested: recorded replay of sample traffic)
- Should renewal ops own a prequalified list of accounts that are high-fit for SLA attach?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Build a slide deck with 3 visuals: cost-comparison, architecture 1-pager, PoC scorecard template.
- Create a short internal checklist for SEs to capture exact model sizes and quantization profile used in PoC.
- Align with legal on a modular SLA addendum template.

Appendix: PoC scorecard (fields to capture) — copy/paste friendly:
- Workload name, sample size (requests), model, median latency, p95 latency, tokens per request avg, error rate, peak RPS, notes

End of doc.

(Informal draft — designed to be copied into Drive doc and iterated in QBR prep sessions; many sections intentionally concise so CSMs can paste into emails or slides.)
